## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Alleviates part of #72015
    - this isn't a perfect fix (hence "alleviates"), but it's nonetheless a significant improvement
    - this only alleviates half of the issue (poor numerical stability), the other half (FoV change issues) is addressed by [Pizzaandy](https://github.com/Pizzaandy)'s #119680 

## Additional information

This PR significantly improves the stability of directional shadows when far from the world origin.

4.5-stable:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dba363a7-1207-4469-bb36-19ba64a920e6

This PR:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e016a20a-ce92-41d0-8364-9af43c7235b8

## Review Notes

### There's a Refactor in Here

This PR refactors a good chunk of the `_light_instance_setup_directional_shadow` function. I initially didn't want to do this,  but I tried many times to tweak the old code and make it work and I wasn't able to, so eventually I gave up and basically rewrote it using the old code as reference.

Part of the reason for this is that this PR (and its refactoring) is a prerequisite for another PR (#119867) which further modifies this code to improve GPU-side directional shadow performance.

As a fun side-effect of the refactoring, the code is now shorter than it was before.

### Larger Shadow Pancake

This PR introduces further padding between the shadow camera's "base" position, and the rendering position. Basically it increases shadow pancaking by a variable amount to help keep shadows more stable:

```cpp
// Snap z to very coarse steps to prevent flickering caused by z changing despite x and y being correctly pinned to a grid point.
light_view_frustum_rect_max.z = Math::snapped(cam_basis_z.dot(frustum_centroid_world) + frustum_circumscribing_radius * 2, frustum_circumscribing_radius) + pancake_size;
```

The PR would still improve the stability without this, but wouldn't be as stable due to the Z axis not being pinned at fixed intervals.

To disable variable shadow pancaking, replace the above line with the following:

```cpp
light_view_frustum_rect_max.z = cam_basis_z.dot(frustum_centroid_world) + frustum_circumscribing_radius + pancake_size;
```

Depending on whether having such large pancaking is a problem, the snap size could be reduced to smaller values if necessary (like half or quarter of the frustum radius).
